papers.title: External validation of a deep-learning algorithm for perimetric glaucoma detection on color fundus photographs in the Rotterdam Study.
papers.authors: van Meyel SWF, van Garderen KA, Vermeer KA, de Vries VA, Ramdas WD, Klaver CCW, Lemij HG.
papers.abstract: Purpose To externally validate a deep-learning (DL) algorithm detecting perimetric glaucoma on color fundus photographs (CFPs) in a population-based cohort. Design External validation in a prospective population-based cohort. Participants Participants aged 50-80 years from three Rotterdam Study cohorts. Methods We applied the winning Artificial Intelligence for Robust Glaucoma Screening (AIROGS) challenge algorithm, trained on 101,442 macula-centered CFPs to detect referable presumed perimetric glaucoma. Performance was assessed at eye and participant level, with participant-level cluster bootstrap confidence intervals. Misclassified cases underwent qualitative review. Longitudinal detection was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier analysis. Additionally, paired analyses compared macula- with disc-centered CFPs. A post-hoc analysis examined the effect of image quality on positive predictive value (PPV). Main outcome measures Sensitivity at 95% specificity, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), partial AUC (pAUC) for 90-100% specificity, PPV, and precision-recall AUC (PR-AUC). Results Among 19,088 eyes (9,837 participants), 201 eyes (1.1%) had perimetric glaucoma. At eye level, sensitivity at 95% specificity was 70.6% (95% CI: 63.8-76.8), with an ROC-AUC of 0.911 (95% CI: 0.887-0.934) and a PR-AUC of 0.343 (95% CI: 0.274-0.427). At participant level, sensitivity was 68.8% (95% CI: 61.8-75.9) and ROC-AUC 0.909 (95% CI: 0.882-0.934). Overall, this resulted in 5.1 referrals per detected glaucoma case. True positives showed more advanced visual field damage than false negatives (median mean deviation -10.8 vs -5.8 dB; P Conclusions The DL-algorithm achieved meaningful discrimination for perimetric glaucoma in an external population-based dataset. Correctly identified cases were frequently flagged at an earlier examination, years before the perimetric diagnosis. Despite having been trained exclusively on macula-centered CFPs, the DL-algorithm showed no loss of discriminative performance on disc-centered CFPs. Incomplete ONH visibility was an important source of false positives. These findings support CFP-based deep learning as a scalable triage tool for glaucoma screening and highlight image acquisition standards for implementation.

papers.title: Defining the optimal duration of remote home tonometry for accurate characterization of intraocular pressure fluctuation.
papers.authors: Jensen MS, Renschler AW, Johnson C, Steel CM, Eddington D, Pizarro Peñaranda MC, Optom SCB, Hamilton N, Nam Y, Wong VW, Kanter J, Johnson TV, Wirostko BM.
papers.abstract: Purpose To determine the minimal duration of remote intraocular pressure (IOP) monitoring needed to yield accurate IOP fluctuation metrics in patients. Design Secondary modeling analysis of retrospective data, validated with a large national database. Participants 397 patients from the Moran Eye Center and/or Wilmer Eye Institute and 1,579 patients from a MyEyes Corporation TM database who utilized an iCare HOME/HOME2 tonometer and recorded ≥3 measurements throughout each day over several consecutive days. Methods Bootstrapped progressive day-censorship analyses and exponential decay modeling were used to estimate the number of monitoring days required to achieve 95% of the maximal model-based reduction in error for IOP metrics, including mean, maximum, range, and standard deviation (SD). Ground truth for each metric was defined using all available measurements within each eye-specific monitoring period. Sensitivity analyses assessing the effects of diagnosis, treatment, and three daily IOP measurements were also completed. Main outcome measures Mean absolute error (MAE) and mean relative error (MRE) for IOP mean, maximum, range, and SD; the number of monitoring days required to achieve 95% of the maximal model-based reduction in error. Results Across both datasets, approximately 6-7 monitoring days were required to achieve 95% of the modeled reduction in error for daily mean, maximum, range, and SD of IOP in the primary analysis. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated longer monitoring requirements in primary open-angle glaucoma (9.1-10.0 days) compared with glaucoma suspects (5.5-6.7 days), secondary open-angle glaucoma (6.4-8.0 days), and primary angle-closure glaucoma (7.8-8.3 days). Monitoring durations remained relatively consistent before and after selective laser trabeculoplasty (8.4-9.0 days) and Hydrus microstent implantation (6.0-6.8 days). Restricting measurements to only three daily IOP recordings throughout the day extended monitoring duration to approximately 10 days in the Moran/Wilmer dataset and longer in the MyEyes dataset. Additionally, 74.1% of peak IOP measurements occurred outside typical clinic hours. Conclusions Remote tonometry provides clinically meaningful characterization of IOP metrics beyond traditional office-based measurements. Depending on the clinical context, seven to ten consecutive monitoring days consisting of measurements across each day are needed to represent a patient's true IOP pattern.

papers.title: Correlation of initial treatment with time to resolution of HLA-B27-associated acute anterior uveitis.
papers.authors: Ruiz-Lozano RE, Pandey A, Pantaleon-Garcia J, Albini TA, Llop SM, Davis JL.
papers.abstract: Purpose Evaluate the treatment outcomes of oral prednisone in HLA-B27-associated acute anterior uveitis (AAU). Design Retrospective single-center clinical cohort study. Participants 462 eyes (462 subjects) with HLA-B27-associated AAU seen at Bascom Palmer Eye Institute between 2014 and 2025. Methods Treatment strategy of the first observed AAU episode was categorized as topical corticosteroids (TCS) plus oral prednisone (TCS+PRED, n = 74), or TCS only (n = 388). Collected data included demographics, ocular findings, and treatment type and duration. The outcomes were analyzed by Kaplan-Meier plots with log-rank tests, hazard ratio (HR), and 95% confidence interval (CI) calculations. Forest plot analysis with Cox proportional hazard modeling was used to compare treatment groups and multiple baseline predictor variables. Main outcome measures Time from treatment initiation to complete control of inflammation (grade 0 anterior chamber cells) and time from treatment initiation to medication discontinuation. Results TCS+PRED significantly decreased the median time from treatment initiation to achieving complete control of inflammation compared with TCS only (28 days [95% CI: 24-35 days] vs. 41 days [95% CI: 35-44 days], P Conclusions Patients with HLA-B27-associated AAU treated with TCS+PRED had earlier control of anterior chamber inflammation despite the probable selection bias for oral steroids to be used in cases with more severe initial presentations. Extending treatment with prednisone for longer than 14 days did not improve results.

papers.title: Changing Patterns of Dry Eye Disease Management in Korea: A Nationwide 10-Year Analysis.
papers.abstract: Purpose To investigate long-term trends in treated dry eye disease (DED) prevalence and medication prescribing patterns in Korea using a nationwide mandatory insurance claims database. Design Retrospective nationwide clinical cohort study. Participants Patients identified from the Korean NHIS mandatory claims database (2014-2023). Methods DED was defined by at least one relevant ICD-10 diagnosis code together with at least one prescription for a DED-related topical medication within the same calendar year. Annual overall, sex-specific, and age-specific prevalence was calculated using the corresponding mid-year resident population. Medication classes and single-use versus multi-use formulations were evaluated. Medication use in Sjögren syndrome-associated versus non-Sjögren DED was compared using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age and sex. Main outcome measures Annual treated DED prevalence, medication prescribing proportions, formulation-specific prescribing trends, and differences between Sjögren syndrome-associated and non-Sjögren syndrome DED. Results Approximately 61.8 million patient-years were analyzed, representing 9.87 million unique patients. Annual treated DED prevalence ranged from 4.84% to 5.61% and was consistently higher in women and older individuals. Hyaluronic acid (HA) remained the most prescribed medication, although its proportional share declined from 85.03% in 2014 to 76.89% in 2023 (P Conclusions Over the past decade, DED management in Korea shifted toward the anti-inflammatory cyclosporine, the mucin and water secretagogue diquafosol, and preservative-free single-use formulations. Patients with Sjögren syndrome-associated DED demonstrated distinct prescribing patterns, including substantially greater cyclosporine use after adjustment for age and sex.

papers.title: Industrialization drives convergent microbiome and host physiological shifts in the human metaorganism.
papers.authors: Poyet M, Rühlemann M, Schaan AP, Ma Y, Moitinho-Silva L, Wacker EM, Jebens H, Patel L, Nguyen LTT, Zimmer A, Plichta D, McDonald D, Stevens C, Agyei A, Afihene MY, Asibey SO, Awuku YA, Badiane AS, Corzett C, Deme A, Dominguez-Rodrigo M, Duah A, Fezeu A, Froment A, Gibbons S, Girard C, Hooker J, Ibrahim F, Iqaluk D, Juimo V, Kettunen P, Lafosse S, Lango-Yaya E, Lee SC, Lehtimäki J, Lim YAL, Mabulla A, Mahachai V, Mohamed RS, Moniz K, Mwikarago IE, Nartey YA, Ndiaye D, Noel M, Onyekwere C, Pin TM, Plymoth A, Roberts L, Ruokolainen L, Rusine J, Segurel L, Shapiro BJ, Sigwazi S, Sistiaga A, Valles K, Vatanen T, Vilaichone RK, Rosenstiel P, Baines J, Franke A, Ellinghaus D, Knight R, Daly M, Xavier RJ, Alm EJ, Groussin M.
papers.abstract: Understanding how industrialization reshapes the human metaorganism requires integrating microbiome ecology with host physiology across globally diverse populations. Here, we generate multivariate data from the Global Microbiome Conservancy cohort, including gut microbiome, immunoglobulin A (IgA) sequencing, host genotyping, diet, lifestyle, and fecal biomarker profiles, to investigate host-microbiome interactions across gradients of industrialization and geography. We show that industrialization is associated with homogenized microbial compositions, reduced microbial diversity, and lower community stability, independent of host confounders. We further show that industrialization is linked to elevated markers of gut stress, increased IgA secretion, and altered patterns of IgA-bacteria interactions. Finally, we show that microbiome-based disease predictors trained on industrialized populations are uninformative in less industrialized cohorts, highlighting limited cross-population transferability. Together, our results reveal coordinated restructuring of the microbial ecosystem and host physiology and emphasize the need for inclusive, globally representative data to improve translational microbiome applications across diverse human populations.

papers.title: Convergent genomic evolution of human gut bacteria along an industrialization gradient.
papers.authors: Rühlemann M, Ma Y, Szánthó LL, Waschina S, Moitinho-Silva L, Mews LC, Faus-Camarena J, Jebens H, Costa J, Juimo V, Fezeu A, Agyei A, Afihene MY, Asibey SO, Awuku YA, Duah A, Nartey YA, Ibrahim F, Lim YAL, Tan MP, Onyekwere C, Rusine J, Mwikarago IE, Baines J, Franke A, Szöllősi GJ, Xavier RJ, Alm EJ, Groussin M, Poyet M.
papers.abstract: Whether human-associated environments drive adaptive genome evolution in gut commensal bacteria remains largely unknown. Here, we investigate how genomic adaptation in gut bacteria differs between industrialized and non-industrialized human populations. We generated a collection of isolate genomes spanning diverse host geographies, lifestyles, species, and strains. We first found that, compared with metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), paired isolate genomes recover more functional elements and signals of horizontal gene transfer (HGT). Leveraging isolate genomes from multiple species, we find that strains from industrialized hosts experience an expansion of proteome size and harbor greater pangenome fluidity, driven by recent HGT events. Gene- and variant-level analyses reveal convergent patterns of lifestyle-specific adaptation in functions that are critical for ecological adaptation, such as the stress response, cell-envelope remodeling, and central metabolism. Our results demonstrate that industrialization drives convergent genome evolution in gut bacteria, providing a framework for understanding the mechanisms of microbial adaptation to rapidly changing human environments.

papers.title: Fatty acid desaturation controls cellular fate decisions between senescence and ferroptosis.
papers.authors: Kuehnemann C, Jezak ST, Mogck BA, Kura N, Tariq R, Che Y, Vaittinen M, Siokas I, Deshpande S, Guthrie C, Tan X, Aimontche E, Kahn AA, Reifsnyder P, Lee G, Majidipur A, Kung AH, Wang Q, Jurk D, Zheng T, Greenberg AS, Wang XD, Kitazawa K, Dolnikowski G, Cheng Y, Matthan NR, Ramanthan A, Lee J, Roh D, Chen HH, Pihlajamaki J, Korstanje R, Wiley CD.
papers.abstract: When subject to damage or stress, cells develop responses in order to maintain tissue homeostasis. Two such responses are ferroptosis and cellular senescence, but how cells decide between these outcomes remains unclear. Here, we show that senescent cells increase import and membrane levels of multiple polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), but a specific intermediate PUFA, dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid (DGLA, 20:3ω-6), is reduced. Exogenous repletion of DGLA instead results in cell death by ferroptosis. Senescent cells manifest additional features associated with ferroptosis, including labile iron and expression of lipoxygenases as well as low-level membrane peroxidation. Oral DGLA supplementation lowers markers of senescence in aged mice and improves age-related functional outcomes. Finally, obese humans with lowered DGLA desaturation rates have lower markers of adipose tissue senescence. Together, our data implicate shifts in PUFA metabolism as a driver of decisions between senescence and ferroptosis.

papers.title: Subsistence transition preceded population turnover in the eastern Colombian Andes.
papers.authors: Sirak K, Delgado M, Triana Vega AV, Rivas S, Argüello P, Boada AM, Rivera-Sandoval J, Peña G, Langebaek C, Ospina JP, Archila S, Torres Orjuela SA, Mejía Cano MB, Rodríguez Saza F, Barton A, Callan K, Curtis E, Frost T, Iliev L, Kearns A, Kellogg J, Lawson AM, Qiu L, Workman JN, Mah M, Nawaz M, Soos G, Cherkinsky A, Hadden CS, Prufer KM, Mallick S, Rohland N, Fehren-Schmitz L, Reich D.
papers.abstract: The Altiplano Cundiboyacense in the eastern Colombian Andes preserves one of the Americas' most continuous archaeological sequences, recording cultural and demographic change. We generated genome-wide data from 212 individuals spanning over 7,000 years, including early-middle and middle Holocene hunter-gatherers, initial late Holocene groups with mixed economies and the earliest isotopic evidence of maize consumption, and increasingly sedentary Herrera and Muisca populations. Individuals predating the Herrera Period form a lineage that persisted for five millennia, structured by drift in small groups without external gene flow. Two individuals dating ∼2,800 years before present (BP) retain autochthonous ancestry while showing isotopic signatures consistent with maize consumption, decoupling subsistence change from population replacement. The emergence of Herrera culture ∼2,200 BP coincided with a sharp genetic break by ∼2,000 BP, which reflects migration by people descended from admixture ∼4,000 BP between groups with Chibchan- and Amazonian-Andean-related ancestries. Herrera and Muisca Period individuals show north-south genetic substructure paralleling archaeological differentiation.

papers.title: TECR palmitoylation triggers a necrotic cell death program driving acute liver injury.
papers.authors: Ru X, Li X, Wu Z, Ren X, Zong Y, Cui Y, Li Y, Ding Z, Wang X, Zhang Z.
papers.abstract: Acute liver injury caused by drug toxicity or immune activation remains a major clinical challenge with limited mechanistic understanding and few effective therapies. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized form of regulated cell death driven by palmitoylation of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-resident enzyme trans-2,3-enoyl-coenzyme A (CoA) reductase (TECR). We show that multi-site palmitoylation of TECR, redundantly catalyzed by the palmitoyl acyltransferases ZDHHC5 and ZDHHC2 and dynamically reversed by the depalmitoylase ABHD10, activates PERK-dependent ER stress signaling to trigger cell death. This cell death pathway is a TECR-dependent, palmitoylation-induced, ER stress-mediated necrotic cell death program (TPNCD). TPNCD contributes to liver injury in mouse models of acetaminophen- and concanavalin A-induced hepatotoxicity and is attenuated by hepatocyte-specific TECR ablation or by pharmacological inhibition of palmitoylation or ER stress signaling. Together, these findings establish TPNCD as a distinct, necrotic cell death pathway underlying acute liver injury and highlight new therapeutic entry points for hepatoprotection.

papers.title: Clonal hematopoiesis and cytopenias following CAR19 therapy.
papers.authors: Hamilton MP, Phillips N, Noordenbos T, Boegeholz J, Sugio T, Sworder BJ, Alig SK, Good Z, Schroers-Martin JG, Tamaresis J, Esfahani MS, Lu Y, Olsen M, Liu CL, Ehlinger Z, Desai M, Muffly L, Negrin RS, Arai S, Johnston L, Lowsky R, Meyer E, Rezvani A, Shizuru J, Weng WK, Shiraz P, Sidana S, Bharadwaj S, Smith M, Dahiya S, Sahaf B, Frank MJ, Mackall CL, Diehn M, Kurtz DM, Miklos DB, Alizadeh AA.
papers.abstract: CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy (CAR19) improves survival in relapsed/refractory large B cell lymphoma compared with immunochemotherapy with intent for autologous hematopoietic cell transplantation (autoHCT). However, major toxicities include prolonged cytopenias, infection and secondary hematologic malignancies. Here, to investigate these complications, we studied patients with lymphoma receiving CAR19 and compared clinical outcomes to propensity-matched autoHCT-treated controls. CAR19-treated patients exhibited impaired immune reconstitution and increased infection. Bone marrow analysis showed that prolonged post-CAR cytopenias are associated with clonal cytopenias of undetermined significance and interferon-mediated inflammation. Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) commonly expanded following CAR19 infusion and was associated with impaired immune reconstitution and treatment-related myeloid malignancy (tMN). Post-CAR tMN was molecularly and clinically comparable to post-autoHCT tMN. Single-cell DNA analysis revealed mostly independent CH clones, while CAR integration into CH-mutant T cells occurred frequently and may drive expansion and persistence. Together, these findings implicate CH expansion and marrow inflammation in key CAR19-associated toxicities.
